findings: The frozen repository context contains three equivalent Java sleep-versus-wait questions and explicitly emphasizes lock release. The answer stays on that comparison and does not dilute it with unrelated thread-pool or lock taxonomy material.

Java SE 26 Thread.sleep supports the candidate's duration/scheduler boundary, current-thread behavior, monitor-retention rule and interruption semantics; Java SE 26 Object.wait and JLS 26 §17.2 support monitor ownership, wait-set membership, release/reacquisition, notification, interruption, timeout and spurious-wakeup semantics.

The most important interview boundary is stated precisely: sleep releases no monitors, while obj.wait releases synchronization claims on obj only, not every monitor held by the thread. This avoids the common but incorrect shorthand that wait releases all locks.

The answer correctly explains that notify/notifyAll does not directly hand over the monitor. A waiter must be awakened and then reacquire the object's monitor before proceeding, which connects monitor mechanics to the reason condition predicates must be protected consistently.

The candidate correctly uses a while-loop predicate around wait because the Object API permits spurious wakeups and because a condition may change before a waiter reacquires the monitor. It also correctly states that both sleep and wait can throw InterruptedException and that the interrupted status is cleared by the documented exception path.

The selection guidance is appropriately bounded: sleep is presented as deliberate delay/backoff, wait/notify as monitor-based condition coordination, and higher-level java.util.concurrent tools only as an engineering alternative for complex protocols. No production incidents or performance numbers are fabricated.

The one-minute section has five crisp comparison dimensions and seven targeted followups. The three-minute material is considerably longer than a literal recital, so oral quality is scored 4/5 while the structured content itself remains complete and source-grounded.
